cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD's name. The psalm says, "Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to Your name be the glory…" (Psalm 115:1). It says "Not to us…" twice, like it really wants to be sure we heard. The credit goes up, not back to the people praying.

The answer is His loving devotion and faithfulness. The psalm says the glory goes to His name "…because of Your loving devotion, because of Your faithfulness." (Psalm 115:1). The reason is who He is. It isn't a thank-you for anything we did.

The answer is in heaven. The psalm says, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). The nations ask where He is, and the psalm answers in one short line, friends. No long speech needed.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "Our God is in heaven; He does as He pleases." (Psalm 115:3). Nobody else decides what He does. The decision is His.
The answer is True. The psalm says, "Their idols are silver and gold, made by the hands of men." (Psalm 115:4). People made them. Silver and gold, and still made by hands.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "they have eyes, but cannot see…" (Psalm 115:5). The eyes are there, but they don't work. It's like a timer with a face and no tick.

The answer is that they become like them. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them…" (Psalm 115:8). The verse also says the same of "…all who trust in them." The psalm doesn't spell out how they become like them, so I'll leave it there, friends.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "Those who make them become like them, as do all who trust in them." (Psalm 115:8). It's not only the makers. All who trust in the idols are included.

The answer is their help and shield. The psalm says, "O Israel, trust in the LORD! He is their help and shield." (Psalm 115:9). Help and shield, two jobs in one line. Compare that to idols that can't even clear their throats.

The answer is the house of Aaron and those who fear the LORD. After Israel, the psalm calls out "O house of Aaron…" and then "You who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 115:10-11). Each call ends the same way: "He is their help and shield." Three groups, one LORD to trust.
The answer is small. The psalm says, "He will bless those who fear the LORD—small and great alike." (Psalm 115:13). Small and great are both covered. Nobody gets left out for being too little.
The answer is True. The psalm says, "May the LORD give you increase, both you and your children." (Psalm 115:14). The blessing covers the listeners and their children. Both are in the prayer.

The answer is the Maker of heaven and earth. The psalm says, "May you be blessed by the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth." (Psalm 115:15). The One blessing you is the One who made everything. The idols were made by hands, and He made the heavens.

The answer is mankind. The psalm says, "The highest heavens belong to the LORD, but the earth He has given to mankind." (Psalm 115:16). The heavens are His, and the earth is given to mankind. That's a big gift, friends.

The answer is we who are still here. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). The line right before says the dead don't praise Him. So "we" is the voice of the psalm.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "But it is we who will bless the LORD, both now and forevermore." (Psalm 115:18). It's now and forevermore. There's no stopping point in that line.
